chapters.title: Chapter 3: How Property Makes and Loses Money

lessons.title: The True Cost of Buying: Stamp Duty, Registration, GST and Brokerage

children.text: Rahul and Sneha finally agree on a ₹1 crore resale flat in Wakad, Pune. The bank has approved an ₹80 lakh loan, and they have ₹20 lakh saved. Done, they think. Then the real bill arrives: ₹7 lakh in stamp duty, ₹30,000 in registration, over ₹1 lakh in brokerage, loan and legal fees, society transfer charges, and a flat that needs painting and repairs before they can move in. They are more than ₹12 lakh short, and the bank will not lend them most of it. This lesson makes sure that never happens to you.

body.text: The price on the agreement is not what a property costs. Budget roughly 8% to 12% on top, mostly paid in cash on day one, and remember that every rupee of it must be recovered through appreciation before you make any profit.

body.label: What stamp duty is charged on
body.value: The agreement value or the circle rate value, whichever is higher
body.context: Paying a lower price on paper does not lower your stamp duty below the circle rate. Registering a sale below the circle rate can also trigger income tax consequences for both buyer and seller.

body.title: Which value counts?
body.question: A flat in Dwarka, Delhi is agreed at ₹90 lakh. Its value at the government circle rate is ₹95 lakh. A male buyer pays 6% stamp duty. How much stamp duty does he pay?
options: Nothing until the flat is resold
body.explanation: Stamp duty is charged on the higher of the agreement value and the circle rate value. 6% × ₹95 lakh = ₹5.7 lakh.

body.title: The women's concession in Mumbai
body.prompt: A ₹1.2 crore flat in Borivali, Mumbai is registered in a woman's sole name, so stamp duty is 5% instead of 6%. Registration is capped at ₹30,000 either way. How much does she save compared with a male buyer, in ₹ lakh?
body.explanation: Male buyer: 6% × ₹1.2 crore = ₹7.2 lakh + ₹30,000 = ₹7.5 lakh. Woman buyer: 5% × ₹1.2 crore = ₹6 lakh + ₹30,000 = ₹6.3 lakh. Saving: ₹1.2 lakh. The concession only applies when she is the genuine owner, which has real legal and tax consequences, so it should never be used as a paper arrangement.

children.text: As you saw in Chapter 2, GST applies only to under-construction homes: 5% for most flats and 1% for affordable housing. A ready-to-move flat with an Occupancy Certificate, or any resale flat, carries no GST. Watch out for GST on other charges, though: brokerage, loan processing fees and some developer charges like club membership attract 18% GST.

In resale deals, brokers typically charge each side around 1% to 2% of the deal value, plus 18% GST if the broker is GST-registered. On a ₹1 crore flat, 1% plus GST is ₹1.18 lakh. When buying a new flat directly from a developer, the buyer usually pays no brokerage because the developer pays the channel partner, although that cost is often built into the price.

body.text: Most of these costs must be paid from your own savings. Banks generally lend against the property's agreement value, not against stamp duty, registration, brokerage or interiors. Your real cash requirement is the down payment plus nearly all of the extra charges, not just the down payment.

body.title: Rahul and Sneha's round trip
body.prompt: Rahul and Sneha's buying transaction costs are stamp duty ₹7,00,000, registration ₹30,000, brokerage ₹1,18,000, loan processing ₹25,000, legal ₹15,000 and society transfer ₹25,000. If they later sell at the same ₹1 crore and pay 1% brokerage plus 18% GST, what is their round-trip cost, in %? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: Buying costs: ₹7,00,000 + ₹30,000 + ₹1,18,000 + ₹25,000 + ₹15,000 + ₹25,000 = ₹9,13,000. Selling brokerage: ₹1,18,000. Total: ₹10,31,000 ÷ ₹1,00,00,000 = 10.31%. The flat's price must rise more than 10% just for them to break even, before counting any tax on gains.

body.text: Compare that 10.31% with equity: buying and selling ₹1 crore of a Nifty 50 index fund costs a tiny fraction of that. It is why property works best as a long holding, and why "buy now, sell in two years" plans rarely make money after costs. At 5% a year appreciation, Rahul and Sneha need about two years just to recover the round trip.

columns.label: Legal ways to save

Negotiating brokerage, or buying directly from the developer
Comparing loan processing fees and asking for waivers
Checking whether affordable housing GST or state first-home schemes apply
Buying a ready-to-move flat to avoid GST

columns.label: "Savings" that backfire
points: Showing a lower price on paper and paying the rest in cash, which is illegal
Registering in a woman's name only on paper, without real ownership
Skipping registration and relying on an unregistered agreement
Using an unregistered power of attorney instead of a sale deed
Skipping legal checks to save a lawyer's fee

body.text: An "under-valued" deal with a cash component does not really save you money. Stamp duty is still charged on at least the circle rate value, the cash is unaccounted income for the seller, and a lower registered price means a lower cost for you when calculating capital gains on a future sale. It also exposes both parties to tax penalties. You will study cash components and circle rates in detail in Chapter 4.

body.label: One more obligation for buyers
body.value: Deduct 1% TDS on purchases of ₹50 lakh or more
body.context: When buying property worth ₹50 lakh or more from a resident seller, the buyer must generally deduct 1% tax at source from the payment and deposit it with the government. It is not an extra cost, but missing it can lead to interest and penalties.

body.title: Maharashtra's minimum value
body.textWithBlank: In Maharashtra, the government's minimum property value used for stamp duty is called the ready ___ rate.
body.explanation: Maharashtra publishes ready reckoner rates every year. Delhi and UP call the same idea a circle rate, and Karnataka and Tamil Nadu call it a guideline value.

body.title: Meenakshi's ₹75 lakh budget
body.scenario: Meenakshi, a 34-year-old doctor in Chennai, has ₹15 lakh in savings and loan approval of ₹60 lakh. She is shortlisting resale flats in Velachery priced at ₹75 lakh, reasoning that ₹15 lakh plus ₹60 lakh equals ₹75 lakh.
body.prompt: What is wrong with her budget, and what price range should she actually be looking at?
body.modelAnswer:
1. She has forgotten transaction costs. Using Tamil Nadu's roughly 9% for stamp duty and registration, a ₹75 lakh flat carries about ₹6.75 lakh in government charges alone.
2. Brokerage at 1% plus GST adds about ₹0.89 lakh, and loan, legal and documentation fees add more.
3. Banks will not fund these charges, so they come from her ₹15 lakh, which leaves too little for the down payment.
4. A rough rule: if government charges, brokerage and other fees total about 10.5% to 11%, the flat price she can afford is about ₹75 lakh ÷ 1.107, or roughly ₹67 to 68 lakh.
5. She should also check that the bank's loan-to-value limit on the lower price still leaves her down payment within her savings, and keep an emergency fund rather than spending every rupee.
6. Practical step: shortlist flats around ₹65 to 68 lakh, confirm the exact stamp duty and guideline value on the Tamil Nadu registration portal, and get written quotes for brokerage and loan fees.

body.title: Build Your True Purchase Budget
steps: Check your state's current stamp duty and registration rates on the official registration portal
Find the circle rate or ready reckoner value for the property and use the higher value
Ask for GST, parking, floor rise, club and deposit charges in writing for new flats
Agree brokerage in writing, and add 18% GST
Get the bank's processing, legal and valuation fees
Add society transfer fees, repairs, interiors and shifting
Confirm how much of the total the bank will actually lend, and fund the rest from savings
Keep an emergency fund aside after all of the above

points: Budget roughly 8% to 12% above the agreement value for stamp duty, registration, brokerage, fees and move-in costs.
Stamp duty and registration are state levies, ranging from about 6% to 9% or more of value, charged on the higher of agreement and circle rate value.
Several states, including Maharashtra, Delhi, UP and Haryana, offer lower stamp duty for women buyers.
Banks generally do not fund these extra costs, so your cash need is the down payment plus most of the charges.
Round-trip costs above 10% make short-term flipping unprofitable; in our Pune example, prices had to rise 10.31% just to break even.
Save legally through genuine ownership concessions, negotiated brokerage and fee comparisons, never through cash components or paper arrangements.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not legal, tax or investment advice. Stamp duty, registration fees, cesses and concessions are set by each state, change often and depend on property type, location and buyer. Always confirm current rates on the official state registration portal and consult a qualified property lawyer, a tax professional and a SEBI-registered investment adviser before buying.
